newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian shares off one pct ahead of May expiry.
newsitem.headline: Austrian shares off one pct ahead of May expiry.

text.p: Austrian shares ended almost one percent lower on Thursday after the onset of late selling pressure and traders said the market looked vulnerable ahead of the expiry of May ATX futures on Friday.
Weak bonds and a generally unfavourable international environment also contributed to the decline, dealers said.
The blue-chip ATX index closed 12.08 points down at 1,249.39 points with 14 shares lower, six higher and one unchanged. May ATX futures were 10.4 points down at 1,247.7.
"Selling orders came in towards the close. Nevertheless I do not see May ATX futures expiring below 1,240 unless Wall Street has a very bad night," a trader said.

Creditanstalt preference shares topped turnover, rising 2.4 schillings to 508 on 187,136 contracts after Bank Austria said it expected to finalise an exchange offer to Creditanstalt shareholders by the end of September.
Bank Austria preference shares, in contrast, were 8.35 schillings down at 413.3 despite news that operating profit, including Creditanstalt, rose 18 percent in the first four months of this year.
Analysts said it was too early to judge the success of the tie-up. They also noted investors were adopting a wait-and-see approach ahead of a planned summer capital increase.

Brickmaker Wienerberger rallied to a high of 2,410 schillings after the firm announced the sale of its Vienna Business Park office and retail complex. Its shares closed four schillings down, however, at 2,330.
"The euphoria faded quickly, which I do not really understand," a trader said.
Analysts welcomed the move, which they said cleared the way for future acquisitions in Wienerberger's core business.
Top gainer was brewer Brau Union which finished 26 schillings, or 3.71 percent, up at 727 ATS after parent company BBAG announced a 69 pct surge in 1996 pre-tax profit on Wednesday.
The broad-based Vienna bourse index fell to 464.08 points from 468.13.
